title: Local skill-validation ranking versus shifted deployment is a model-selection-under-distribution-shift object unless a skill-specific structural residual survives
dead_end_scope: The standalone PA-05 claim that a high rate of family-level ranking inversion or deployment regret between SkillEvolBench T1-T3 local replay validation and T4-T6 shifted deployment identifies a new skill-evolution selection-validity problem merely because the compared persistent representations are distilled skills versus raw trajectory reuse.

counter_explanation.statement: The frozen PA-05 statistic is exactly a source-to-target model-selection comparison under deliberate distribution shift. Its local selector observes the T1-T3 within-environment performance difference between two representations, while its oracle is defined by the T4 context-shift, T5 adversarial, and T6 composition performance difference. Ranking reversal and oracle-versus-local regret are therefore direct predictions of ordinary validation/deployment mismatch, domain shift, and conditional treatment-effect heterogeneity whenever source-domain performance is not invariant for the target roles. Matching the latent family and comparing the same two arms removes family difficulty and global-arm confounding, but it does not change this statistical object: the remaining representation-by-role interaction is precisely the effect modification a generic distribution-shift or domain-generalization model is allowed to express. Naming the two arms raw trajectory reuse and distilled skill memory does not create a distinct selection principle.
counter_explanation.opposite_prediction: With the same T1-T3 outcomes, family identity/features, role definitions, and any other pre-deployment observables, a generic source-to-target model-selection or conditional-domain-shift model predicts that local ranking is reliable only to the extent that the arm effect is invariant or predictably transports to T4-T6. It permits arbitrary family-conditioned ranking reversals and positive selector regret when that invariance fails. Replicating the reversal on seed B reduces execution-noise uncertainty but still does not distinguish a skill-evolution mechanism from this mature reduction. If additional pre-deployment shift or representation features predict the reversal, the same-information generic conditional selector can use them as effect modifiers unless a structural restriction makes a different ex-ante prediction.
counter_explanation.opposite_principle: Validation performance identifies deployment-optimal selection only under an appropriate transport/invariance relation between the validation and deployment distributions; a ranking reversal across deliberately shifted task roles is a model-selection-under-distribution-shift phenomenon unless an additional structural constraint yields a prediction that the same-information shift model cannot represent.
counter_explanation.opposite_search_seed: Reuse SkillEvolBench only to search for a preregistered representation-specific structural variable that remains decision-relevant after matching all T1-T3 local outcomes, family/role observables, target-shift descriptors, model, token/call budget, and execution order. The next candidate must state an ex-ante pairwise prediction that a same-information distribution-shift/domain-generalization selector cannot express—for example an independently measured information-loss or executable-constraint property of the persistent artifact whose intervention changes T4-T6 transfer while local evidence and generic shift features remain matched. Do not reopen from another validation/deployment ranking inversion, larger selector regret, a different seed, or another model alone.
counter_explanation.scope: PA-05-SKILL-VALIDATION-TRANSFER on SkillEvolBench arXiv:2605.24117 / first-party repository commit 9e3daa339987c3cfa624121e1be442593a53d43c, specifically the preregistered T1-T3 local-selector versus T4-T6 deployment-oracle inversion/regret F0. This adjudication does not claim that SkillEvolBench lacks useful mechanistic phenomena; it closes only ranking inversion/regret as the standalone scientific novelty.
alternative_explanations_ruled_out: Family difficulty is the only explanation: the F0 matches both arms within each latent family, but a within-family representation-by-role interaction remains exactly a conditional/domain-shift effect and therefore does not escape the mature reduction.

A best-global-arm baseline closes the reduction: beating or tying a single global arm only measures whether one fixed decision is adequate; it does not distinguish the local selector from generic conditional model selection under shift.
Seed noise is the scientific mechanism: seed-B replication can establish that a ranking reversal is reproducible, but reproducibility does not make validation/deployment mismatch a new causal object.

Persistent skills make the selection problem intrinsically new: persistence changes the candidate representations being selected, but the frozen PA-05 statistic contains no additional lineage, update, or artifact variable that makes a different ex-ante prediction from source-to-target model selection.

T4-T6 are merely more difficult versions of T1-T3: the benchmark explicitly changes context, adversarial pressure, and composition role; whether this is called difficulty or shift, the F0's scientific endpoint is still cross-role transport of relative performance, which generic conditional shift models express.
counter_explanation.reopen_condition: Reopen only with a preregistered same-information residual in which the candidate and the strongest distribution-shift/domain-generalization selector receive identical T1-T3 outcomes, family and role observables, representation metadata, target-shift descriptors available before T4-T6 outcomes, model, execution order, calls/tokens, and compute, yet a skill-specific structural variable forces different ex-ante arm-selection predictions and the difference is validated by an intervention or independent executable truth. Ranking inversion, selector regret, seed replication, global-arm controls, or changing the backbone without such a structural residual is insufficient.

fresh_phenomenon_closure.closure_scope: T1-T3 local-validation versus T4-T6 shifted-deployment ranking inversion and selector regret as standalone novelty only

scientific_interpretation.safe_claim: SkillEvolBench remains a strong first-party executable substrate for studying procedural representation transfer, but the current PA-05 success criterion would only establish a reproducible local-validation/deployment ranking failure under deliberate shift. That is useful diagnostic evidence, not a standalone new self-evolution principle.
